articles.title: Bateria do notebook: deixar na tomada o dia todo faz mal? | G1
articles.standfirst: A bateria tem vida útil limitada mesmo sem uso, mas a forma como você carrega o notebook pode acelerar ou evitar esse desgaste.
articles.summary: Veja o que acontece com a bateria ao deixar o notebook na tomada o dia todo e entenda os riscos para o aparelho a longo prazo.
articles.body:
Deixar o notebook na tomada o dia todo estraga a bateria? — Foto: TheRegisti/Unsplash

De forma geral, deixar o notebook na tomada o dia todo não vai desgastar mais a bateria do que deixá-lo passar pelos ciclos de descarregamento e carregamento.

Mas isso não é consenso entre as marcas e pode ter outras consequências, como diminuir a vida útil dos outros componentes, caso o dispositivo fique ligado por longos períodos.

🔋 O que acontece com a vida útil da bateria se ficar na tomada o dia todo?

É importante entender que a vida útil da bateria gira em torno de dois principais fatores: o tempo de vida dos componentes e os ciclos de carga e descarga aos quais ela é submetida.

“Estando em operação ou não, as baterias têm um tempo de vida limitado”, afirmou Bruno Lima, coordenador do curso de engenharia da computação da Universidade Presbiteriana Mackenzie, em entrevista ao g1 em 2025.

Segundo o engenheiro, dependendo do fabricante e da qualidade dos componentes, essa durabilidade "pode variar de 2 a 3 anos”. Ou seja, mesmo sem uso, a bateria sofre desgaste natural ao longo do tempo.

Mas o número de vezes que você carrega e descarrega normalmente o dispositivo – chamadas de ciclos – também pode influenciar a longevidade dele. Conforme aumenta a quantidade de ciclos, a bateria não tem mais o mesmo desempenho.

Em notebooks mais antigos, a bateria continuava sendo consumida mesmo com o aparelho na tomada. "Em modelos mais novos, o sistema consome a energia direto, sem passar pela bateria ", disse Ricardo Ciuccio, coordenador do curso de engenharia da computação do Centro Universitário Senac.

“O fato de ele estar sempre na tomada vai fazer com que essa bateria retenha a carga. Não vai ter um efeito significativo no tempo de vida além dos ciclos normais de carga e recarga ”, explicou Lima.

No entanto, os especialistas chamam atenção para os efeitos negativos para as outras partes do computador.

“Quando você deixa ele ligado por dias, você está mantendo os componentes energizados, está passando corrente, ele está aquecendo. Isso pode degradar a vida útil dos componentes”, explica Lima.

Ciuccio aponta que o calor gerado pela bateria com a carga completa pode também danificar os componentes. "Quando está carregada, esse calor vai tirando uma fração de tempo da durabilidade da bateria", comentou.

"É aí que tem divergências entre fabricantes. Você vai encontrar manuais que são favoráveis a manter o notebook na tomada e outros que não são", completou Ciuccio.

📄 Sempre confira a recomendação da fabricante

Além do panorama apresentado pelos engenheiros, vale checar quais são as recomendações da fabricante, pois as orientações podem variar conforme a marca e o modelo do aparelho.

Em seu site, a Lenovo afirma que “manter a bateria conectada por longos períodos não fará com que ela seja sobrecarregada”.

Mas faz um alerta: “Se a bateria permanecer carregada em ou próximo a 100%, a Lenovo recomenda configurar o recurso Battery Charge Threshold para limitar a carga.”

Segundo a marca, isso minimiza a degradação desnecessária . A Lenovo ainda recomenda definir o limite superior de carga para 80% ou menos.

A Dell segue na mesma linha, afirmando que não há problema em manter o aparelho na tomada, mas com algumas precauções.

“É uma boa prática desconectar o notebook da tomada de vez em quando para permitir que a bateria passe por ciclos de descarga e recarga, o que também pode ajudar a manter a saúde da bateria”, comentou a fabricante, em nota.

Já a HP aconselha contra o uso do dispositivo na tomada por longos períodos. Segundo a marca, isso pode fazer com que a bateria perca sua calibração e capacidade de carregar corretamente.

A HP orienta que o usuário deixe a bateria do notebook descarregar completamente de tempos em tempos e, em seguida, volte a carregá-la totalmente, para ajudar a mantê-la calibrada.

💡 Dicas práticas para preservar a vida útil da bateria do notebook

Segundo Bruno Lima, um dos maiores responsáveis de danos à bateria do notebook é o impacto físico, causado por quedas ou batidas.

“Não pode ter impacto de forma alguma . A bateria, na verdade, é um conjunto de metais com um eletrólito, onde acontece uma reação química que gera energia”, explica Lima.

“Se você derruba, acaba danificando essa estrutura; elas acabam se aproximando, rolando ou rompendo e perdem a capacidade de carga”, completa.

Lima também aponta que temperaturas extremas podem afetar a bateria de forma parecida com o impacto físico, já que a dilatação pelo calor ou a retração pelo frio causam movimento dos componentes.

Já Ciuccio avisa que é preciso tomar cuidado com a adequação do carregador . Pegar um carregador emprestado, especialmente quando é de outra marca, pode fazer mal à saúde da bateria, mesmo que tenha a mesma entrada.

Portanto, não é recomendável usar carregadores que não sejam originais e feitos para o seu produto.

"Tem um problema de interface de tensão, que pode fazer a sua bateria sofrer um pouquinho", comentou Ciuccio. " E se o cabo estiver torcido, danificado, pode até ter fuga da corrente e você não conseguir carregar a bateria. "

Os engenheiros dão algumas dicas de como cuidar da bateria e prolongar sua vida útil:

Evite deixar o notebook no sol ou apoiar sobre a cama, para não esquentar.

Evite descarregar o notebook por completo muitas vezes.

Se a bateria zerou, deixe carregar até 100% antes de tirar da tomada.

Os primeiros sinais de que a bateria está no fim da vida útil incluem o estufamento – quando ela fica visivelmente inchada – e a perda de velocidade no carregamento.

articles.title: The investigation into Tesla Autopilot’s emergency vehicle problem is getting bigger
articles.summary: The investigation into Tesla Autopilot is now affecting the automaker’s rivals. NHTSA sent requests to 12 major car companies, including Ford, GM, VW, and Toyota, requesting information into their Level 2 driver assist systems.
articles.body: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is requesting advanced driver assist data from 12 automakers as it seeks to expand its investigation into Tesla’s Autopilot. The government is probing a dozen incidents involving Teslas crashing into emergency vehicles. According to Automotive News, the agency’s Office of Defects Investigation sent letters to a dozen major automakers, including Ford, General Motors, Toyota, and Volkswagen, requesting information regarding their Level 2 driver assist systems, in which the vehicle can simultaneously control steering, braking, and acceleration under specific circumstances. Automakers are being asked to provide the number of vehicles with Level 2 systems that have been manufactured in the US, as well as the total number of miles covered with those systems engaged and a recent list of any changes or updates. NHTSA is also requesting customer complaints, field and crash reports, and any lawsuits related to the Level 2 systems. The data request comes less than two weeks after NHTSA sent an order to Tesla to provide data on the operation of its Autopilot system, including details on which of its sold vehicles are equipped with Autopilot as well as the system’s operating parameters. The agency’s investigation into Tesla could have wide-ranging implications for Tesla, which has pushed the boundaries in releasing experimental software to untrained customers in order to advance its vision of autonomous driving. NHTSA’s investigation covers an estimated 765,000 Tesla vehicles that were released from 2014 through 2021. The agency is looking into 12 crashes in which Tesla owners using the company’s Autopilot features have crashed into stationary emergency vehicles, resulting in 17 injuries and one fatality. Most of these incidents took place after dark, with the software ignoring scene control measures including warning lights, flares, cones, and an illuminated arrow board. Tesla has until October 22nd to hand over the data. US-based automakers like Ford, GM, and Stellantis have until November 3rd, and all other car companies, like Toyota, Subaru, Nissan, and Honda, have until November 17th. Automakers that fail to respond could face civil penalties of up to $115 million. A spokesperson for Toyota said the company would comply with NHTSA’s request. A VW spokesperson declined comment, while media contacts for the other automakers did not respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: The original smart oven goes dark.
articles.summary:
Today, Weber shut down June Oven’s cloud servers, leaving ovens that cost up to $1,500 unable to do anything beyond basic functions.
Owners were notified in July that September 22 would be the end, cutting off remote control via the app, live camera viewing, AI food recognition, and software updates. The ovens still work through their built-in touchscreens, including local food recognition, but support for repairs and parts is also done.
Weber bought June in 2021 and quickly discontinued the ovens, folding June’s technology into Weber Connect. It says it won’t open-source the app because the IP is used in current and potentially future products.

articles.title: Boat launches smart earbuds range with Crest AI; offers Airdopes Prime 800 D, Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Nirvana Ion ANC earbuds
articles.summary: Audio News: Boat has launched its first smart audio devices range featuring Boat Crest AI, its AI-powered platform built with Google Gemini. The lineup includes B.
articles.body: Boat has launched its first smart audio devices range featuring Boat Crest AI, its AI-powered platform built with Google Gemini. The lineup includes Boat Airdopes Prime 800, Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC. With the launch, Boat is introducing a new proposition for personal audio — ‘Intelligent Ears’ — earbuds designed not just for listening, but to listen, understand, converse and assist.In a press release, the company said that the Crest AI is built around a simpler idea: bringing intelligence to something consumers already wear throughout their day — their earbuds. At the heart of the experience are three capabilities — Crest Ask, G- Assist and Crest Translate, or simply: Ask. Assist. Translate.With Crest Ask, users can ask questions, explore ideas, learn and have natural conversations with AI. Instead of repeatedly reaching for a phone or typing a query, users can ask follow-up questions and continue the conversation through their earbuds.With G- Assist take the experience from conversation to action. With integration across Google Gmail, Tasks, and Calendar, users can access everyday productivity and communication capabilities through voice. From asking the assistant to “summarize my day” to “reply to an email,” G-Assist helps users manage tasks, stay on top of schedules, and interact with their digital routines without reaching for their phones.Crest Translate enables real-time, two-way translation across 25+ languages, helping people speaking different languages communicate more naturally.Gaurav Nayyar, CEO, Boat said “Why should intelligence be limited to our rooms, desks, pockets or screens? We believe it can become much more natural and simply be with you. With Crest AI, built with Google Gemini, we are bringing that intelligence to your ears. Our idea of ‘Intelligent Ears’ is simple: earbuds that can listen, understand, converse and assist. But this is just the beginning, we are working on multiple other use cases. For ten years, Boat has helped India listen. Now, we want to help India listen, understand, converse and assist”.The Boat Airdopes Prime 800 D combines Crest AI capabilities with Dolby Audio and 11mm dynamic drivers tuned to Boat Signature Sound. The earbuds offer up to 45 hours of total playback, Multipoint Connectivity and four microphones with AI-ENx technology, bringing together entertainment, communication and intelligent assistance in one device.Crest AI is also available on the Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC. articles.title: Simon Cowell to miss America’s Got Talent Season 21 finale amid health concerns; KSI to replace him on judges’ panel
articles.summary: Simon Cowell will not be part of the America’s Got Talent Season 21 finale as he continues to recover from a medical procedure for his ongoing back pr.
articles.body: Simon Cowell will not be part of the America’s Got Talent Season 21 finale as he continues to recover from a medical procedure for his ongoing back problems. The veteran judge and creator of the NBC talent show had been away from the live episodes in recent weeks and was initially hoped to return before the season came to an end.However, Simon will now remain absent for both parts of the finale, which are scheduled to air on September 22 and September 23. His absence means viewers will see a different face occupying his usual spot on the judges’ panel as the remaining contestants compete for the Season 21 title.YouTuber, musician and boxer KSI has been chosen to join the panel for the finale. He will sit alongside Howie Mandel, Sofia Vergara and Mel B during the final performances as well as the results episode. KSI is not new to the Got Talent franchise. He previously appeared as a judge on Britain’s Got Talent, giving him experience with the format and its high-pressure auditions.Simon stepped away from America’s Got Talent in August while dealing with his back-related health issues. Following his procedure, fellow judge Howie Mandel had shared an encouraging update, saying he had been told that the treatment had gone well and that Simon was doing okay.Earlier, Howie had also expressed hope that Simon would recover in time to return for the moment when the new winner of the competition was announced.While Simon has been away, the show has continued with a series of guest judges filling in at different stages. Among those who have joined the panel are actor and comedian Kenan Thompson and former America’s Got Talent judge Heidi Klum.The Season 21 performance finale is scheduled for September 22 at 8 p.m. ET on NBC, with the results episode following on September 23 at 9 p.m. ET.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: Motorola showcases Signature 27 with 50MP main camera and 200MP periscope telephoto camera
articles.summary: Tech News News: Motorola has showcased the Signature 27, its second smartphone in the Signature series and one of the first phones announced with Qualcomm’s latest Sn.
articles.body: Motorola has showcased the Signature 27, its second smartphone in the Signature series and one of the first phones announced with Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. The smartphone was unveiled at the Snapdragon Summit 2026 on Tuesday and comes with a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera and a 200MP periscope telephoto camera. Motorola is also changing its naming system with this phone, using the final two digits of the upcoming year for its new generations. The company has not yet announced the price or exact sale date, but says the Signature 27 will launch globally later this year.Motorola Signature 27 featuresThe Motorola Signature 27 is powered by Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor. Motorola says the chipset brings improvements to on-device AI, camera performance, gaming response and download speeds. The phone also comes with Motorola’s ArcticMesh cooling system. It combines diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal and copper mesh with a redesigned 3D vapour chamber. Motorola says the new vapour chamber is 40% larger than the previous generation.Motorola Signature 27 gets a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera along with a 200MP periscope telephoto camera. Motorola has also introduced its Video Enhancement Engine, which uses AI to study a scene before and during video recording and adjust colour tones in real time.The phone will also support Google's Gemini Omni, which can use prompts, photos or existing video clips to create a finished video. Google's Lyria can be used to generate music and soundtracks.The phone will be available in Pantone Coal Smoke and Pantone Capulet Green. The Coal Smoke version has a woven texture designed to improve grip and durability, while Capulet Green gets a brushed, textile-inspired finish.Motorola Signature 27 operating systemMotorola says the Signature 27 will receive seven years of OS upgrades and is expected to launch with Android 17. It is also the company's first smartphone with Audio by B&O, with the branding etched onto the rear panel.Motorola has not yet revealed the phone's display, battery capacity, charging speed, RAM, storage or other camera sensors. articles.title: Xiaomi’s new 18 Pro phones improve on Samsung’s privacy display
articles.summary: An international launch for the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max is confirmed for later this year.
articles.body: Xiaomi’s new 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max launched in China today, and feature a more flexible take on the privacy display tech introduced this year on Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra. They combine it with returning rear screens, two 200-megapixel cameras, and both of Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chips. A global launch is confirmed for later this year — especially welcome since last year’s 17 Pro phones skipped international markets. The two 18 Pro phones look similar to the 17 Pros, with similar compact displays built around the rear cameras, capable of displaying notifications, taking selfies, playing simple games, and more. The bigger changes are to the front screen, which is now equipped with hardware-level privacy features much like the S26 Ultra’s. Xiaomi’s implementation looks smarter than Samsung’s though: when you activate it for a specific app, it will not only turn on when that app is opened, but apply to notifications, floating windows, and split-screen views, without affecting the rest of the display. Location-based triggers allow you to set it to turn on when you reach work, or off when you come home, with smart triggers for when it detects locations like airports or elevators. It can also use the selfie camera to detect prying eyes and suggest activating the privacy mode. [Image: [Image: [Image: The two phones differ in size, with a 6.4-inch display on the Pro and 6.9 inches for the Pro Max. Battery varies accordingly: 7,000mAh or 8,500mAh respectively, using a high 32 percent silicon content. The other difference between the two is the chipset, with the Snapdragon 8 Gen 6 Elite in the Pro and the Extreme version in the Pro Max, though differences between the two chips are slight. Cameras are led by a 200-megapixel main camera using a large 1/1.28-inch-type sensor (the Light Fusion 960 in the Pro, and 960L in the Pro Max, though they seem similar). A 200-megapixel, 75mm telephoto joins it, the same on both phones, using Samsung’s 1/1.56-inch HP5 sensor and with a minimum focus distance of 12cm. A 50-megapixel ultrawide completes the trio. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Xiaomi’s launch follows similar announcements this week for the Vivo X500 and Oppo Find X10 flagships. The two 18 Pro phones start from ¥5,999 (about $900), and join the 18 Fold in Xiaomi’s new flagship lineup, but we’re still waiting for the regular Xiaomi 18 and the 18 Ultra, likely to appear next spring. An international launch for at least one 18 Pro phone will come later this year, though we’re still waiting to hear if the Fold will ever leave China.

articles.title: FCC chair blasts House Democrats 'extreme position' on gender ideology in kids' programming in fiery letter
articles.summary: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr fired back at House Democrats who opposed the agency's push to reform children's TV ratings over content pushing gender ideology.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX — The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr on Tuesday issued a fiery response to the opposition from House Democrats over the agency's effort to reform television ratings for children's programming, some of which promotes gender ideology. In April, the FCC issued a public notice seeking feedback about parents' concern about the content of shows their children watch, suggesting the current ratings system is outdated and deems "shows with transgender and gender non-binary programming as appropriate for children and young children" and that new ratings may be necessary. That prompted a response in June from Democrats on the Congressional Equality Caucus, who accused the FCC of wanting to "censor the inclusion of transgender characters or topics" from children's programming and said that the current ratings system is "satisfactory and overwhelmingly popular among parents." WASHINGTON FATHER SUES SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR DENYING RELIGIOUS OPT-OUT FOR 5TH GRADER FROM LGBTQ INSTRUCTION "We strongly believe that parents should decide what their children watch on television," the lawmakers wrote. "Programs should not have higher ratings or content warning simply because of the identity of the programs’ characters. Applying higher ratings or content warnings because of a character’s gender identity would be harmful to transgender people and transgender acceptance and would harken back to a time when politicians sought to censor television programming because they included minorities." The House Democrats continued, "Any attempt by FCC to censor content because it includes transgender characters or topics would raise both legal and constitutional concerns... Any attempt to issue rating warnings for depictions and themes related to transgender people would also raise concerns of content-based and viewpoint discrimination in violation of the First Amendment." BLUE STATE SCHOOL DISTRICT ACCUSED OF DEFYING SUPREME COURT, HIDING GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS In a letter sent Tuesday to Congressional Equality Caucus Chair Rep. Mark Takano, D-Calif., Carr expressed regret for the stance the Democratic lawmakers had taken. "I am deeply concerned by the position that you and over 60 of your Democrat colleagues in the House of Representatives are taking regarding the right of parents to know whether their sons or daughters are being exposed to controversial gender identity ideologies—including the promotion of transgender and gender non-binary programming—in television shows that are rated as appropriate for young children," Carr began the letter obtained by Fox News Digital. "In your letter, you come out swinging against both transparency and common sense," Carr added. "You stake out the radical position that parents have no right to know whether controversial gender identity ideologies are being promoted in children’s television programming. In your view, parents should not be empowered to make informed choices about the programs their children watch." Carr called the Democrats' defense of transgender people an "extreme position" which he said comes as children's programming is "secretly promoting gender ideology to young kids without the knowledge or consent of their parents." He went on to list several examples of gender ideology appearing in children's programming, citing an episode of Disney Jr.'s "Muppet Babies" reboot (TV-Y) where Gonzo wants to dress as a princess instead of a knight, calls himself "Gonzo-rella" and is referred to in the episode with the "they" pronoun, as well as a trans character in Netflix's "Strawberry Shortcake: Berry in the Big City" (TV-Y) and pansexual and non-binary characters in the Disney Channel's animated series "Primos" (TV-Y7). "Keeping parents in the dark about the nature of these programs is a feature not a bug of the effort. Indeed, you write in your letter that 'many recognize their gender identity at a young age.' And you appear to suggest that informing parents would prevent 'self-acceptance,'" Carr wrote. "Recent studies show a massive spike in younger people identifying as transgender with some attributing this to media exposure. But your position that New York and Hollywood programmers should have a direct line to children without parental knowledge is at total odds with the law Congress passed." "Opposing transparency puts you on the wrong side of the issue. Parents are nearly unanimous in wanting to know what their children are watching and to determine for their own families what shows are appropriate. Despite your opposition, the FCC will continue its work to empower parents and continue to engage with stakeholders as part of the agency’s open and ongoing proceeding," Carr added. articles.title: LinkedIn is cracking down on fake employees.
articles.summary:

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Simon Cowell: ‘Failures aren’t great to go through, but you learn from them,’ a powerful life lesson on how setbacks are not stopping points but stepping stones

articles.body: Failure is never an option for most people, as it can lead to disappointment, frustration and the feeling of having tried your hardest and it still not being enough. However, one of Simon Cowell’s quotes serves as a gentle reminder that even the shiniest successes and the most anticipated events can tarnish with time. The only way to avoid this is to embrace failure as part of the learning process.Motivational quote of the day by Simon Cowell: ‘Failures aren’t great to go through, but you learn from them.’What is the meaning of the quote of Simon Cowell?The quote by Simon Cowell, “Failures aren’t great to go through but you learn from them,” signifies that although failures could be dreadful experiences, individuals can always learn from them. From the quotation, one can understand that rather than giving up on a task, one should question the reasons for failing and use the insight to do things right in the future.Why is the quote of Simon Cowell relevant today?The saying is relevant because, to this day, people experience failures in various aspects of life. Failure could be in career, academics, relationships, business, or even art. Whenever one faces a challenge, it could be disheartening and disappointing to think that the efforts put into a venture could have been futile. Nonetheless, Cowell’s quote provides a different perspective on failures because when one is unsuccessful in certain undertakings, it does not imply that they will never be successful. Therefore, one should reflect on their failures and use the insights to be more careful in the future endeavors. The quotation is also significant to the contemporary society because individuals like Cowell are more interested in the outcomes of their actions.Early life of Simon CowellSimon Phillip Cowell was born on October 7, 1959, in London, England, and he was raised in Elstree, Hertfordshire. His father was Eric Cowell, a music business executive and property developer, while his mother was Julie Cowell, a former ballet dancer and socialite. Cowell attended Dover College before leaving school at sixteen.After leaving school, Cowell worked several jobs before entering the music industry. His father helped him get a job in the mailroom at EMI Music Publishing. He eventually moved into A&R, where he began developing his experience in identifying and working with musical talent.His early career also included setbacks. Cowell went on to form Fanfare Records, which initially found success but eventually collapsed in 1989. The setback left him in financial difficulty and he moved back in with his family. He later returned to the music business as a consultant for BMG and gradually rebuilt his career.Simon Cowell’s rise to fameHis major television breakthrough came with Pop Idol in 2001. The show’s success was followed by American Idol, which premiered in the US in 2002, where Cowell became known for his direct judging style. articles.title: Eight Sleep's new Pod 6 comes in smaller and solo sizes, starting at $1,999 | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Eight Sleep said the new pod is 20% faster than the previous generation.
articles.body:
Sleep tech company Eight Sleep on Wednesday launched its new Pod 6 device in a smaller size than previous editions to fit more bed frames, along with solo sizes for one-person use. The company said that the device can be used to adjust the temperature on either side 20% faster than the previous-generation gadget.

Because the new pod has a 50% smaller footprint, it can fit most bed frames. The company claims the device has 9x more sensors, enabling it to understand granular temperature controls for each user even if they are sleeping close together. Plus, it can ignore data from a pet or a kid sleeping on the bed with two users.

The Pod 6 is available starting today in over 37 countries, starting at $1,999 for solo sizes and $2,699 for standard sizes. Solo sizes can fit a twin bed and one side of queen, king, and California King beds. Standard sizes will be available in queen, king, and California King. Plus, it can work with existing add-ons like a blanket, pillow cover, and base.

Beyond new sleep products, the company is pursuing Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval to transition its Eight Sleep Pod into a regulated medical device for sleep apnea in the U.S.

Earlier this year, the company raised $50 million from Tether at a $1.5 billion valuation . Eight Sleep also took steps to expand its international footprint by launching its product in China, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Singapore in the last year, with China becoming one of the fastest-growing regions.

The company’s CEO Matteo Franceschetti told TechCrunch that international markets contribute over 30% of revenue. He mentioned that the sleep tech company plans to expand into other regions of Asia and Latin America. Franceschetti noted that the company is keeping a keen eye on the component crunch in the electronics sector, but didn’t say whether it will impact pricing.

“We definitely see the market changing a little bit because AI companies are requesting a lot of different components. We are adjusting our supply chain [to counter that]. It’s definitely something that we need to watch out for, particularly as our devices become more and more, I would say, compute-heavy and intelligent to be able to provide AI features to our users,” he said.

articles.title: This $199 GPS sports watch is repairable, modular, and open-source
articles.summary: The $199 Una Watch says it’s the first GPS fitness smartwatch that’s modular and repairable, with open-source hardware and software.
articles.body: The Una Watch costs less than most Garmin watches now that its price has been lowered from the Kickstarter offer of $350 to $199, but its modular, repairable design grabbed my attention first. It features a 1.2-inch MIP LCD display and up to 10 days of battery life, similar to the Garmin Forerunner 70 or the Pebble Round 2 I preordered earlier this year. Like Pebble’s revamped watches, the Una Watch is also open-source, including its SDK, housing, and circuit boards, but it has more fitness features out of the box than Pebble’s watches currently offer. Una is also encouraging users to build their own apps for it, including with vibe coding — it says users can “ask an AI coding assistant to interpret Una’s developer documentation, produce code, diagnose errors and refine the resulting application.” Una says every component in the watch is “accessible with a standard tool,” so users can repair or upgrade it themselves. The open-source mechanical components also open the door for users to design and 3D print their own accessories or mods for it, like converting it into a cycling computer. It features dual-frequency GPS, 24/7 heart rate tracking, a barometric altimeter, a six-axis accelerometer and gyroscope, a three-axis magnetometer and a replaceable 280mAh battery with USB-C charging. However, the Una Watch is only IPX5 splash- and showerproof, not fully waterproof.

articles.title: Logitech’s new Blue Yeti 2 mic adjusts itself to where you are
articles.summary: Logitech G’s Blue Yeti 2 USB microphone builds on its predecessor’s classic design with some modern upgrades.
articles.body: The original Blue Yeti has been one of the most recognizable go-to USB microphones for content creators since it launched in 2009, and now it finally has a successor. Launching today under Logitech G, the Blue Yeti 2 adds some modern upgrades, including an interactive LED display, AI de-noising, and a proximity based voice sensor — which resolves a notable flaw with its predecessor’s design while still paying homage to it. It’s available in black or white color options for $159.99, which is comparatively cheaper than Shure’s popular MV7 series USB microphones, which are the current choice for podcasters and start at $299. It’s also interestingly just $10 more than the original Blue Yeti’s launch price 17 years ago. A lot has happened since then, with Logitech acquiring the Blue audio production company for $117 million in 2018 and later killing the Blue brand entirely in 2023 when it merged the products with its own gaming-focused Logitech G sub brand. That means this new launch should just be called the Yeti 2, but Logitech clearly has some nostalgia to play with here. [Image: If you prefer to manually adjust your gain and other audio settings then this image suggests you can do so. The Blue Yeti 2 includes a built-in audio proximity sensor that tracks your voice in 3D, and automatically adjusts gain, EQ, and pickup patterns to preserve recording quality regardless of how close or far you are when moving around the mic. That should make this a more beginner friendly USB microphone than the original, as you don’t need to have any knowledge or experience with manually tweaking those settings to achieve optimal results. Plus, it still retains a similar design to the OG Yeti which confused people into incorrectly speaking into the top of it, an issue this new sensor should address. [Image: [Image: It provides up to 24-bit / 48 kHz high-resolution capture. Other audio features include integrated direct digital signal processing (DSP) to improve voice clarity without additional software, and AI-powered noise removal to reduce unwanted background sounds like computer fans and mouse clicks. Given Logitech is pitching this to streamers, the 1.3-inch color LED display on the front where the controls are located also features a “Yeti character” that provides visual feedback on gain levels and polar patterns.

articles.title: She'd rather work for Rupert Murdoch than stay at CNN. Here's why
articles.summary: Bay Area tech journalist and podcaster Kara Swisher says she plans to leave CNN rather than work under David Ellison once the merger between Paramount and Wa...
articles.body:
Kara Swisher has reached a breaking point with one of the biggest media deals of the year.

The Bay Area tech journalist and podcaster says she plans to leave CNN rather than work under David Ellison once the merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery is complete.

Ellison is CEO of Paramount Skydance, which has been cleared to merge with Warner Bros. Discovery after reaching a deal with California Attorney General Rob Bonta that was announced Monday, Sept. 21.

"I'd rather work for Rupert Murdoch," Swisher, referring to the controversial media mogul who owns Fox News, told author and academic Scott Galloway on her "Pivot" podcast.

Swisher went on to call Ellison and his father, Oracle CEO Larry Ellison , "terrible media owners" and said she's already asked her agent if could get out of her contract with the cable news network earlier. The agreement runs through the end of the year.

"It's only a few months, right?" Swisher said on the podcast episode that dropped Tuesday, Sept. 22. "I just can't. I was trying to figure out ways I could work with them in some like licensing way. But then I thought, 'F- these guys.' I don't want to work for them. I just don't."

Bonta had been leading a 12-state coalition that included 11 other attorneys general in a lawsuit that was intended to block the $111 billion merger, but has agreed to drop the lawsuit after Ellison agreed to certain concessions intended to preserve film and television production schedules.

Ellison is working to complete the merger by Oct. 1. The deal would combine Paramount's holdings - including Paramount Pictures, CBS, Showtime and the Paramount+ streaming service - with Warner Bros. Discovery's entities such as Warner Bros. Pictures, HBO, CNN and the streaming service HBO Max.

Many observers note that CNN may drastically change if Ellison places controversial CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss in charge of the 46-year-old network founded by Ted Turner as the first 24-hour news channel.

"They've been very nicely trying to keep me, and I have a lot of regard for the executives there now," Swisher said. "But I am not staying. I have other things that make more money, that matter more, that have a bigger audience."

Swisher and Galloway are scheduled to bring a live version of the "Pivot" podcast to the Golden Gate Theatre in San Francisco on Nov. 7.

articles.title: Microsoft’s new Surface Mouse has haptic feedback and a customizable action button
articles.summary: The $79.99 Surface Mouse will start shipping on October 13th.
articles.body: Microsoft is launching a second generation of its Surface Mouse next month that includes haptic feedback support. The Surface Mouse also has a customizable action button for the first time, which is primarily designed for quick access to Copilot (of course), but can be configured to work with other shortcuts from the Surface app. “Its haptic feedback adds a small, purposeful physical response to the moment you usually only see on a screen: a click registering, a window snapping into place or an object aligning just right,” says Brett Ostrum, corporate vice president of Surface Devices. “It is subtle by design, but noticeable within seconds — and hard to give up once you have it.” The haptic feedback works with things like clicks, drags, and alignment throughout Windows 11, but the tactile feedback also triggers in apps like PowerPoint, Affinity, Concepts, and Filmora. Microsoft added support for haptic feedback in Windows 11 earlier this year, and so far it’s mainly Microsoft and Logitech that are supporting it with dedicated hardware. Logitech’s MX Master 4 has haptic feedback, and its Pro X2 Superstrike (and today’s new X3) includes a haptic-based clicks system that doesn’t support the Windows 11 haptic feedback. The upcoming Surface Laptop Ultra also has a haptic trackpad. After originally launching the Surface Mouse in 2016 and not updating it since, Microsoft has now redesigned it to be more comfortable for all-day use, with a soft-touch material at the top. Thanks to Bluetooth 6.0 support, you can now also pair it with up to three devices. The new Surface Mouse will be available on October 13th, the same day Microsoft launches its refreshed Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch devices. It will be priced at $79.99, and available in black and platinum color options.

articles.title: Microsoft refreshes its smaller Surface Pro and Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus
articles.summary: Microsoft is refreshing its Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch. The hardware remains the same, but the chips get upgraded to Qualcomm’s X2 Plus.
articles.body: Microsoft is refreshing its Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch devices with Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon X2 Plus chips. The smaller Surface devices retain the same design and hardware features from last year, with faster and more capable chips inside and higher price tags (thanks RAMageddon!). While the 12-inch Surface Pro started at $799.99 last year, it’s debuting on October 13th at a starting price of $1,149.99. Likewise, the 13-inch Surface Laptop was originally priced at $899.99, but it’s up to $1,199.99 this time around. There’s no base 8GB model this time, causing some of the price increase, as both devices launch with a minimum of 16GB of RAM and can be configured up to 24GB. Pricing aside, Microsoft is promising that the six-core Snapdragon X2 Plus chips will deliver up to 18 percent more efficient battery performance, more than 60 percent faster graphics performance, and up to 95 percent faster local AI inferencing on the built-in NPU. [Image: That’s a lot of percentages, but what it equates to on these devices is better battery life and improved performance. On the Surface Pro 12-inch Second Edition, as Microsoft calls it, that means an extra hour of web browsing (up to 13 hours in total), and on the Surface Laptop 13-inch Second Edition it’s two extra hours of web browsing usage (up to 18 hours in total). Microsoft is using similar displays on these models as last year, so the Surface Pro 12-inch has a 2196 x 1464 (220 PPI) LCD display that runs at up to 90Hz. The Surface Laptop 13-inch still ships with a 1920 x 1280 (178 PPI) display that only runs at 60Hz. Both displays have been upgraded from 400 nits of brightness to 500 nits, though. Port selection remains the same, too. Both devices include two USB-C 3.2 ports, and the Surface Laptop 13-inch also has a USB-A 3.2 port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. Both also support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity. I’m surprised that Microsoft hasn’t upgraded at least one of these smaller Surface devices with a haptic trackpad, particularly because Windows 11 now adds subtle haptic nudges, and the Surface Laptop Ultra ships with haptic feedback. Microsoft is launching a second edition of its Surface Mouse with integrated haptics, and you can read all about that here. Microsoft is also bringing back the black color option for both of these smaller Surface devices, with platinum silver or violet colors available too. Both devices will also be sold to commercial customers, and the Surface Pro 12-inch will be available in an optional 5G configuration.

articles.title: Jeff Garlin Says ‘Undiagnosed Bipolar’ Made Him ‘Mean’ on ‘The Goldbergs’ Set; Wendi McLendon-Covey Responds: ‘I Remember Things Differently’
articles.summary: Jeff Garlin revealed in a recent interview on The Daily Beast’s “Obsessed” podcast (via Entertainment Weekly) that he had undiagnosed bipolar disorder during...
articles.body:
Jeff Garlin revealed in a recent interview on The Daily Beast's "Obsessed" podcast (via Entertainment Weekly ) that he had undiagnosed bipolar disorder during the making of ABC's "The Goldbergs," which he notably exited from after an HR investigation into multiple claims of inappropriate conduct against him. The 1980s-set family sitcom, which ran for 10 seasons and 229 episodes from 2013 to 2023, starred Garlin opposite Wendi McLendon-Covey. Garlin exited in 2021.

"At the time, I was undiagnosed bipolar," Garlin said on the podcast, noting he got his diagnosis after exiting the series. "I was miserable on the show, and I was miserable with my performance. And [Wendi] was always trying to tell me, 'Hey, you're really great on the show.' I didn't believe her. I just got to the point where I had to quit, and she was very resentful."

Garlin added, "Being bipolar, I was either one of three things: dark, dark, dark, dark, didn't talk and look at anyone; happy to the point of mania, never turning off my thing; or mean — really, really mean."

McLendon-Covey reacted to Garlin's comments on Instagram by disputing his comments: "Huh. Let's just say I remember things very differently, as does the crew, the other actors, the writers, and our executives."

When Garlin exited "The Goldbergs" in 2021, two sources close to the production confirmed to Variety that it was a mutual decision between the actor and the network. Shortly before, Garlin addressed allegations against him in an interview with Vanity Fair , acknowledging that an HR investigation into his on-set behavior had been ongoing for the past three years and dismissing a rumor that he had been fired from the series.

"We have a difference of opinion, Sony and myself. Okay. My opinion is, I have my process about how I'm funny, in terms of the scene and what I have to do. They feel that it makes for a quote 'unsafe' workspace," Garlin said at the time. "Now, mind you, my silliness making an unsafe workspace — I don't understand how that is… I am always a kind and thoughtful person. I make mistakes, sure. But my comedy is about easing people's pain. Why would I ever want to cause pain in anybody for a laugh? That's bullying. That's just uncalled for."

The allegations against Garlin ranged from unwanted hugging and touching people on set to telling jokes that made others uncomfortable. McLendon-Covey later said during an interview with Andy Cohen for SiriusXM that Garlin's exit was "a long time coming."

"That it finally happened, it was like, 'Ok, finally someone is listening to us.' But that was kind of hard though because we had lost George Segal in real life," she added. "To have to go through another loss on a sitcom…you can't keep asking your audience to mourn people. That's not why they tune in… I'm exhausted by that topic and the PTSD of it all. I just feel like the less people know about that, the better. No one benefits from knowing anything."

"The Goldbergs" was in the middle of filming its ninth season when Garlin was fired. As Variety exclusively reported at the time, producers decided to keep Garlin's character on the show for the rest of the season by using off-camera dialogue and unused takes pulled from earlier episodes, as well as previously shot images of Garlin. The actor's stand-in was also used in group scenes, but he was shot from the back. The final result was visually awkward and earned so many complaints on social media that McLendon-Covey even weighed in at the time.

"This season threw us for a loop because it's hard to incorporate someone who doesn't want to be there and wants to leave mid-scene, and we weren't about to rewrite the second half of the season," the comedian wrote on Twitter at the time . "We're doing our best."

When "The Goldbergs" kicked off its 10th and final season last fall, the show killed off Garlin's character.

articles.title: Meta ditches the camera on its newest smart glasses
articles.summary: The Ray-Ban Meta Audio Glasses are $349 smart glasses without the camera. Muse is also coming to all of Meta’s glasses.
articles.body: Walking around Meta Connect 2026, everyone’s sporting smart glasses in all sorts of shapes, colors, and sizes. It’s a marked difference here, a tech bubble where “pervert glasses” are not a concern. Outside Connect, the public backlash against wearable surveillance tech — a catchall term that encompasses not just smart glasses, but also smartwatches and AI pendants — is gaining steam. So it’s incredibly curious timing that this year, the company is launching Ray-Ban Meta Audio Glasses: smart glasses infused with Meta AI, but with no camera for recording others. To hear Meta tell it, that’s a coincidence. Audio-only glasses have been years in the making. “Three years ago, it wasn’t clear if AI glasses were going to be a thing. Back then, every other company was backing out of the space,” says Alex Himel, Meta’s vice president of wearables. “Then two years ago, we saw that audio was the top use case, the biggest potential for AI, and that it should work well in a pair of audio glasses.” [Image: There are multiple combinations of colors and lenses across two styles for the audio-only glasses. Clubmaster is in the middle here, sandwiched between two Burbanks. Himel has a point. Open-ear audio is the least controversial part of the Ray-Bans — and the thing everyone can agree is convenient. Plus, the camera-less glasses are lighter. Himel says that by removing the cameras, Meta could “rearchitect” the glasses. “That allowed us to take a lot of electronics out of the front frame and have a lot more design flexibility.” The audio-only models start at 43 grams — heavier than normal wire-frame glasses, but noticeably lighter than the roughly 50g Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2 and the 69g Meta Ray-Ban Display. The arms are thinner. They come in two styles: the Mad Men-esque Clubmaster and the more Wayfarer-reminiscent Burbank. The hinges extend for wider faces; the temple arms and nose pads are adjustable. There are 23 color and lens combinations, and they can support the same wider prescription range as the Ray-Ban Meta Optics lineup. Even more so than the standard Meta Ray-Bans, these look and wear like normal glasses. And with a $349 starting price, they’re cheaper too. Free of a power-hungry camera, the battery lasts an estimated 12 hours on a single charge. The most technical things you can do with them are interact with Meta AI, take phone calls, and listen to podcasts or music. And that’s it. [Image: I think Clubmaster looks fetching on me. But these look like ordinary glasses. “They don’t record,” Himel says. “The only thing they do, which is the same thing as an Alexa device in your house or some other devices, they’re just listening for a specific wake word. They’re not sending anything … If they hear [the wake word], then they start listening to what you’re saying. When you’re done talking, then it’s processing, and that’s visible to the AI. It gets processed, and that’s kind of it.” Slipping them on, they’re comfortable and, I think, quite fetching on me. Regardless of how one might feel about Meta, it’s fair to guess most people would feel less like a creeper wearing these. Meta Glasses and Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 I feel differently slipping on the new Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3. Partly because the camera is back in play, partly because the pair Meta gives me is the new aviator style with transition lenses. I’m told I can pull it off, but I keep asking my colleague Jay Peters if I’m giving ’80s serial killer vibes. The other new style is called Zena — not the warrior princess — and it’s a bolder, geometric cat-eye frame. The third-generation glasses feature fairly minor refinements. There’s a sixth microphone, compared to the second generation’s five, for clearer phone calls. Battery life has gotten a slight boost to nine hours, an hour longer than the second gen. The temple arms, like the audio-only glasses, are adjustable for a better fit. All sound will now be captured in Dolby Atmos for spatial audio. Sure! That’s neat if I’m in my quiet hotel room, but it’s harder to appreciate when reviewing footage amid the hustle and bustle of Meta Connect. The new model comes in 27 color and lens combinations, plus three seasonal options. Along with the hardware changes, the Gen 3 glasses are also getting a price bump. They start at $449, up from $379 for the second-gen models last year. [Image: Teehee, is this 80s serial killer vibes or… Meta Glasses — the off-brand, more affordable entry-level glasses launched a few months ago — also have more options. There are two new styles, Capri and Nova. Capri is some kind of cat-eye shape, while Nova… honestly, the styles are all starting to blur together. They’re round and remind me of several other Ray-Ban Meta glasses, but slightly different. There’s a new ivory-colored Kylie Jenner pair that costs $399. But maybe Kylie Jenner isn’t the celebrity collab you’ve been dreaming about. That’s fine. Because Blackpink’s Lisa — a K-pop icon and The White Lotus actress — also has Meta Glasses. They have pink lenses and come with a blind-box-type charm styled after Lisa’s pets. These also start at $399. (Non-celebrity versions of the Meta Glasses start at $249.) Why the celebrity collabs? Options for more people, including women. [Image: Blackpink (glasses) in your area. “With the Meta Glasses Starfire with Kylie, we saw a younger, more female audience start to buy the glasses,” says Himel. “Wayfarer is the most popular glasses type in the world, but it tends to be more male — though definitely not exclusively male. The second brand we did was Oakley … but Oakley [also] tends to be a more masculine brand. So I think with Kylie and Lisa, and with more styles, we’re seeing them appeal to more women.” There are actually more limited-edition versions, styles, colors, and prescription permutations available across the entire existing Ray-Ban Meta lineup at a whole range of price points. I suspect I’d need to make a spreadsheet to list them all. While scuttling about Meta’s campus this week, I’m brought to an entire area where they’re all displayed. It looks like a high-end store for, regular, schmegular glasses. That, I suspect, is the whole point. AI in your frames All around the campus, there are life-size cutouts of Meta’s cuddly Muse mascot. That’s because Muse, Meta’s recently released personal AI agent, is coming to the seemingly 4,000 iterations of Meta smart glasses that now exist. “Muse is gonna be everywhere,” confirms Himel. “Muse is gonna be on every device that we make.” The pitch for Muse in your glasses is that your AI assistant will better remember your context and do things on your behalf. During a demo, I ask a Muse agent to help me buy snacks that will give me the best protein bang for my calorie buck. It can do it, but fails at adding another snack to my cart. Obviously, this is an early-stage demo, and there are always kinks. I can see the shape of how this could be helpful. I can also see how it’d be a treasure trove of data for Meta. Less contentious is a demo of a new FDA-cleared hearing assistance feature. I’m asked to wear earplugs to mimic mild hearing loss. Things sound a bit muddled. With the feature turned on, higher voices gain a tinny quality as the AI works to boost conversational tones in a semi-loud environment. After about five minutes, I’ve forgotten I have earplugs in. Adding this capability will cost an extra $149, but I’m told it’s FSA/HSA eligible and designed to be a one-time fee versus an ongoing subscription. [Image: The Nova glasses! Lastly, there are two minor privacy updates — though neither truly addresses the fears people have been debating this past summer. The first is bringing the same “private processing” pipeline used on WhatsApp to wearables. It’s a server-based system in which a user’s data is inaccessible to Meta or any other third parties when end-to-end encryption isn’t possible or on-device processing isn’t powerful enough. “It’s so that you know that your data is just yours and you’re the only one who has access to it. Other companies have taken an approach to everything on-device. We do a lot on-device. But the problem with just doing things on-device is that the device is only so powerful and capable. And so if you want to run more capable models and get better functionality, we want to offer the same privacy protections, but with more capabilities. So that’s what private processing is,” says Himel. Meta will also roll out an update where users can opt out of their visual data being used for AI training. (Audio-only queries are still used for training.) That’s progress but doesn’t really address people’s primary concerns about the glasses being used to covertly record people in public. Himel also acknowledges that the private processing feature is mostly about protecting the data of the person wearing the glasses. More is more Meta’s goal at Connect this year is to bombard everyone with options. By the end of the year, Meta expects to have over 100 versions of its glasses. The more versions of its glasses, the more people they’ll reach. The more AI updates that trickle to each of these iterations, the faster Meta can stake its claim on the next era of mobile computing. So goes the theory. But providing hardware options isn’t Meta’s problem. Inside the safe bubble of Meta’s campus, everyone wears these glasses. The issue is outside Menlo Park, where a vocal contingent isn’t asking for more. They’re asking for less.

articles.title: Muse is coming to Meta smart glasses
articles.summary: Meta announced a slate of new features coming to its smart glasses at Meta Connect, including its new AI agent, Muse, and some accessibility updates.
articles.body: Just a couple of weeks after launching Muse, Meta announced that it’s “working on” bringing the agent to its smart glasses, including the new glasses it unveiled at Meta Connect. Users will be able to activate Muse from their glasses by saying its name and ask it to handle tasks like guiding a workout, logging meals, or helping them shop for products they’re looking at. Muse is just one of several major updates coming to Meta’s glasses. They’re also getting some new accessibility features, like a Hearing Enhancement feature Meta says is “FDA-cleared software for adults with perceived mild to moderate hearing loss.” It will be available later this year with a Meta One subscription or as a $149 add-on for compatible glasses. Meta AI will also be able to give “more context-rich answers” when users ask the glasses what they’re looking at, potentially making Meta’s glasses more effective for helping blind and low-vision users interpret their surroundings. A new audio customization feature will also allow users to shift their smart glasses’ volume between their left and right ears, including sending all audio to one side. Meta’s introducing some new audio and photo features as well, including Dolby Atmos Capture, which will allow users to record videos with 360-degree spatial audio. A new Dynamic Photo feature automatically captures multiple frames when you take a photo with Meta’s glasses, then uses Meta AI to suggest the best frame from each batch. The Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses are getting the new “Hologram” feature Meta announced for its new VR Glasses, which it says is “a photorealistic digital version of your face for calls from Meta Ray-Ban Display” that “infers” your expression using your voice. The feature’s “rolling out in Early Access on WhatsApp to Meta Ray-Ban Display users in the US later this fall.” A couple new heads-up navigation features are coming to the Meta Ray-Ban Display as well. Starting later this month, users in the US and Canada will have an option to use their voice to ask for real-time cycling or public transit directions. The Meta Ray-Ban Display will also start using “the world in front of you rather than street signs in turn-by-turn walking directions,” like referencing a house, car, or landmark the glasses detect. A few other new features are on the way for the Display glasses, including an option for editing photos directly on the glasses’ display, a new “Explore” app for finding new apps, an improved calendar, and mirroring for phone notifications.

articles.title: Meta’s next VR device isn’t a headset — it’s glasses
articles.summary: The new Meta VR Glasses, announced at Connect, sit on your ears like a pair of glasses but have immersive displays for watching movies, playing games, and working.
articles.body: Meta is launching new VR hardware: a pair of glasses. The new Meta VR Glasses sit on your ears like a typical pair of glasses instead of being strapped over your head, but they still have immersive displays for watching movies, playing games, and getting work done. Imagine a pair of hefty black sunglasses with blacked-out lenses on the outside, but the components of a typical VR headset distributed between the device on your head and a computing puck in your pocket. The idea is to give you a way to experience VR in a much lighter and more approachable form factor than Vision Pro or Meta Quest-style headsets. I got to try the VR Glasses at Meta’s campus this week, and as Meta walked me through some familiar VR demos like watching content, playing a game, and working from multiple screens, I was impressed by how much lighter the whole experience felt. Some of that was about the literal weight, as the glasses come in at just 100g, far less than the Quest 3’s 515g. But there was also something lighter in a more intangible way: the glasses form factor made the headset seem like something I could easily jump in and out of instead of being a whole cumbersome commitment with big head straps. It felt like a lightweight Vision Pro, and is perhaps a better execution of some of what Apple wanted to do with that device. [Image: The back of the Meta VR Glasses. To keep things light, the VR Glasses’ display and the sensors are all you actually wear on your face. The separate puck connected with a wire contains the guts powering the headset: a Snapdragon Reality Elite processor, 128GB of storage, 12GB of RAM, and the battery, which Meta says will offer up to three hours of media playback, though you can continue using the glasses even while the puck is being charged. The display is what Meta calls a 5K MicroOLED “Infinite Display.” It has 2412 x 2288 pixels per eye at 37 pixels per degree and supports a refresh rate of up to 120Hz. On the front of the glasses are two cameras for color passthrough, letting you see through to the world around you. The headset comes in small and large sizes to offer different options for width, though they cost the same. [Image: Here’s the compute puck. It has a solid clip. You primarily use your eyes and hand gestures to control the glasses. You just look at elements onscreen to navigate, and the OS will highlight what your eyes are looking at using two pairs of eye-tracking cameras. To select something that’s highlighted, you can pinch your thumb and pointer finger together, and to scroll around, you make a fist and move your thumb around the top of your hand. It feels similar to the gestures from the Meta Ray-Ban Display, but those require a neural wristband; the VR Glasses instead use six external cameras to follow your hands. Based on my demos, I think the VR Glasses will be best for entertainment because of the big virtual screen. Meta showed me a clip from James Cameron’s Billie Eilish concert film, which was impressive on a huge virtual display, and parts of the most recent NBA Finals, which was filmed on a format called VR180 that provided a 180-degree view of the court. I also got to watch some of Avengers: Endgame in what Meta characterized as a “VR Enhanced Cinema” experience made in partnership with Disney and Industrial Light & Magic. In the entire VR environment around the screen showing the film, there were graphics that thematically lined up with what was actually happening onscreen that also changed as the clip went on; when a huge energy beam appeared at a major moment in the film featuring Thor, I saw one shoot out at the top of the VR environment, too. Meta says that VR enhanced versions of Avengers: Infinity War and Star Wars: A New Hope will be available when the VR Glasses launch. [Image: Gaming remains a major use case, too. Meta showed me a new mode for Beat Saber called Flux that supports playing with hands (though it will work with the Quest’s Touch Plus controllers, too). Instead of waving virtual sabers to hit blocks in time with the music, like in the original, Flux tasked me with moving my hands, which were each surrounded by balls of energy connected by pulsing electricity, to break through flying poles and smash targets. It makes sense when you play it, and the one song I played was really enjoyable. The VR Glasses will have more than 75 games at launch that will support the new hands-first experience (including a VR version of Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Dual Destinies launching in 2027), but they’ll also support the entire current Quest app catalog and can connect to Touch Plus controllers (and Bluetooth controllers). Meta is also pitching this as a way to browse apps and do some work, and I can see the vision. In one demo, I used the glasses to mirror three windows from a nearby laptop. You’ll be able to connect wirelessly to computers or other devices with a USB-C connection, which could be useful if you want more screen real estate for work. My favorite demo from my whole session was actually one about typing. While using a special version of Instagram made for the VR Glasses, I was prompted to leave a comment on a picture, but I was able to type that comment and navigate the app using a virtual keyboard and trackpad that appeared after I laid my hands flat on the table. To my surprise, the virtual keyboard and trackpad were actually good. Of course, the experience wasn’t as speedy as using a physical keyboard and mouse, but in a pinch for a short message or email, I think it could be quite useful. (I should note it’s not technically new; Meta introduced this for Quest headsets earlier this year, and I haven’t tried it on those devices.) [Media: The glasses cost $1,299.99 and will go on sale in spring 2027. That price puts the VR Glasses between Meta’s $599.99 Quest 3 and a high-end VR headset like Apple’s $3,499 Vision Pro, and I think that’s the right way to think about them. I don’t think they will transform the landscape of VR, especially when Meta itself has been divesting from VR software and largely moving on from the VR version of Horizon Worlds. Meta is still planning to develop full VR headsets, the company’s VP of product for VR, Angela Chang, tells The Verge. But as tech companies chase the next big hardware category, however, a new form factor is starting to emerge: something that’s more capable than most smart glasses but less overbearing than a full-on VR headset. Google and Xreal are teaming up on XR glasses. Snap’s idea is the augmented reality-focused Specs glasses, and Meta is working on AR glasses too. The VR Glasses represent another fascinating idea of what a computer on your head can be.

articles.title: Meta is trying VR glasses (again), this time with more IMAX | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Meta's return to the VR glasses realm comes with a promising combination of light weight form factor and enhanced entertainment options.
articles.body:
Meta is renewing its quest to make virtual reality a thing. At its Connect event on Wednesday, the company announced Meta VR Glasses, its newest entry into the VR market, which will be available next spring starting at $1,299.99.

These glasses actually seem quite promising, thanks to a substantially lighter form factor and a host of new entertainment integrations — including (allegedly) IMAX compatibility.

Moments before unveiling them, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg reminded the audience that the company had decided awhile ago to shift its focus away from the Metaverse and build fewer VR devices until it had real breakthroughs.

“This is a breakthrough,” he exclaimed before showing off the glasses. “A lot of people agree that augmented reality glasses with holograms are clearly going to be part of the future, but we’ve also heard that a lot of people are less interested in wearing a headset. So we have built a new kind of VR device that delivers the same magical feeling of presence and immersion with high-resolution displays and views of the world around you in a form factor that is a pair of glasses for the first time.”

Meta says that the glasses are five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3 — and they look much more like normal eyewear than the bulky headsets the company has released before. The frames are made of magnesium alloy, and the glasses are powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite processor. They connect to a computing puck that doubles as a battery, which users can just slip the puck into their pocket to use the glasses on the go.

The glasses are largely built for entertainment. Micro-OLED panels built into the lenses provide what Meta calls a 5K Infinite Display with 37 pixels per degree, along with Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos audio support. Users will be able to download and watch movies.

Perhaps one of the more unique features of the glasses, however, is that Meta is pitching them as a great way to enjoy IMAX-captured films.

Indeed, the company calls the glasses the “first IMAX-enhanced certified VR device ever” and says they will be one of the few ways to experience the expanded aspect ratio that defines IMAX’s distinct high-resolution viewing experience.

The glasses also support 3D content, including movies that integrate a user’s physical space into their viewing experience. Meta says that it has teamed up with Disney and that in November, Disney+ users will be able to stream specific movies — including certain Marvel movies — in 3D.

Meta says that users will be able to watch specific movies and have their surroundings “transformed with immersive environments, dynamic effects, stunning 3D visuals, and spatial audio” — essentially converting the movie into a VR gaming-type experience.

The glasses will also come with Meta AI — its automated virtual assistant — built in, which means that users will be able to talk to the glasses and automate various tasks via voice command. For instance, Meta says you’ll be able to start a movie just by asking your glasses to do so. Other ways to issue commands include hand gestures.

articles.title: Meta Connect 2026: The 7 biggest announcements
articles.summary: Meta launched a new VR Glasses wearable at its annual Meta Connect event, plus new versions of its AI smart glasses, including one without cameras.
articles.body: Meta announced a slate of new wearables during its annual Meta Connect showcase on Wednesday. The star of the event was the new Meta VR Glasses, which pack virtual reality tech into a lightweight smart glasses-style frame with a tethered puck. Meta also announced new pairs of screen-free smart glasses, along with some new AI features and style and frame options. You can catch up on all the highlights from this year’s Meta Connect below. Meta VR Glasses bring virtual reality to a lighter form factor [Image: Meta’s latest wearable offers full virtual reality in a smart glasses-style form factor. Unlike a typical VR headset, the VR Glasses don’t have any straps, and Meta says they’re “five times lighter than Meta Quest 3” at just 100g. Similar to Google’s Project Aura, the glasses are tethered to a pocket-sized puck with the compute hardware, battery, and storage, including a Qualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite, 128GB of storage, and 12GB of RAM. The 5K micro OLED “Infinite Display” has 2412 x 2288 pixels per eye, with a refresh rate of up to 120Hz. The Meta VR Glasses are launching in spring 2027 for $1,299, pricier than the Meta Ray-Ban Display but less expensive than the Apple Vision Pro, while offering similar features. Users can connect the glasses to a Mac or Windows laptop for use as a virtual external display, with an option for a virtual surface keyboard and touchpad. The VR Glasses also have access to the full Meta Quest catalog of apps and games and support for Xbox Cloud Gaming. Meta says the glasses are “the first IMAX Enhanced certified VR device ever,” and users will be able to watch “immersive live sports” with them as well as 3D movies. They even have a “hologram” feature that creates a “photorealistic digital version of your face” for using in calls while wearing the glasses, reminiscent of the “personas” on the Apple Vision Pro. Meta is launching camera-free smart glasses [Image: The highlight of the Ray-Ban Meta Audio is the feature they don’t have: built-in cameras. You can use them for things like listening to music, taking calls, or chatting with an AI assistant, but they can’t take pictures or record video — features that have sparked privacy and harassment concerns around Meta’s other glasses. Meta says the new audio-only glasses are also its “lightest, slimmest AI glasses yet,” weighing just 43g. They offer up to 12 hours of battery life per charge, or 48 hours with the charging case. The Ray-Ban Meta Audio will launch on October 13th starting at $349 with 23 different color and lens combinations. Refreshed Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 arrive with battery and design upgrades [Image: Meta launched an updated version of its main Ray-Ban Meta glasses, starting at $449. The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 offer up to nine hours of battery life, one hour more than the Gen 2. They also have “a new customizable action button for instant access to Meta AI” and a new six-mic array that Meta says “cuts more than 90% of background noise.” The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 has a slimmer design than the Gen 2 as well, with 27 color and lens combinations, including new Zena and Aviator frame styles. Notably, one thing that hasn’t changed is the built-in LED light that indicates when the glasses are recording, which Meta rolled out a privacy fix for last month. Budget glasses launch along with new glasses styles [Image: Alongside its pricier Ray-Ban glasses, Meta also announced some updates to its in-house line of glasses. It’s launching a new lower-cost version of the Meta Adventurer, which will start at $249 for a basic design with black frames and gray lenses, launching October 23rd. Meta is also introducing a new “Mix & Match” program for customizing its glasses with different frames, lenses, and case colors. Plus, its EssilorLuxottica collection is getting two new styles, Capri and Nova, and the Kylie Jenner Starfire frames are getting a new ivory colorway. Meta’s also launching a new collaboration collection with Lisa of Blackpink. Meta Glasses are expanding to more countries starting today, too, including Singapore, South Korea, Mexico, and the United Arab Emirates, with availability in Brazil “coming soon.” Meta Ray-Ban Display is coming to more regions with some new features [Image: A year after they originally launched, the Meta Ray-Ban Display are coming to more regions. The glasses are on sale in the UK and Canada starting today, and they’ll be available in France, Italy, and Germany starting on October 13th. Meta’s also introducing online ordering for customers in those regions and the US. Meta’s launching a new Explore app for Display glasses where users will be able to “browse and use a growing selection of experiences built for your glasses.” The Meta Ray-Ban Display is also getting photo editing, an improved calendar, and mirrored phone notifications. Plus, Meta says the “hologram” feature launching on its VR Glasses is rolling out on the Meta Ray-Ban Display “in Early Access on WhatsApp to Meta Ray-Ban Display users in the US later this fall.” Meta’s Muse AI is coming to glasses and video calls [Image: After launching its new Muse assistant earlier this month, Meta says it’s “working on” bringing the AI to its smart glasses. When it arrives on the glasses, Muse will be able to do things like guide your workouts, log meals, book appointments, and “help buy products you see.” Meta also announced some new features for Muse, including video calls with a customizable live avatar of the AI. Plus, Muse agents are getting their own email addresses for completing tasks and communicating with users. Meta is making an AI ‘charm’ [Image: Mark Zuckerberg teased one last device, Muse Charm, a small AI gadget that houses the Muse agent and looks a little bit like a supersized Tamagotchi. More details will be shared “soon,” he said, but the product is supposed to ship in time for the holiday season.
