articles.title: Apple Siri settlement: iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 16 owners can now claim up to $95; here's how to file
articles.summary: Apple has opened the claims window for its $250 million (about Rs 2,200 crore) settlement over the delayed Apple Intelligence upgrade to Siri.
articles.body: Apple has opened the claims window for its $250 million (about Rs 2,200 crore) settlement over the delayed Apple Intelligence upgrade to Siri. Eligible iPhone owners in the US can now file for a payout of $25 per device. That figure could rise to $95, depending on how many people come forward.The class action, Landsheft et al. v. Apple Inc., accused the company of selling the iPhone 16 as "built for Apple Intelligence" while the smarter Siri shown at WWDC 2024 was nowhere near ready. That upgraded Siri only reached users with iOS 27 earlier this month, more than two years after its first demo. Apple has denied any wrongdoing, and the settlement terms say it is not an admission of liability.Only US buyers of seven iPhone models qualify for the payoutThe claim covers purchases made between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025. The iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max qualify, along with the entire iPhone 16 lineup: the iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max and the budget iPhone 16e.You must be the original buyer, and the phone must have been bought for personal or work use, not resale. Indian buyers of the same models are not covered, since the case was filed and settled in the US.Filing an Apple Siri settlement claim needs your iPhone serial numberClaims are filed on the official website, SmartphoneAISettlement.com. The form asks for your name, address, phone number and the iPhone's serial number, which you'll find under Settings > General > About. If you don't have the serial number, the form will take your Apple Account email and the phone number linked to the device instead.Eligible owners should also receive an email over the coming days with a claim ID and PIN. You can still file without them. Each device needs its own claim, and only one payment is allowed per phone.The $95 maximum depends on how many iPhone owners filePayouts start at $25 per device and can climb to $95 if fewer valid claims come in than expected. Payment options include PayPal, Venmo, direct deposit and a paper check.Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder of Clarkson Law Firm, described the fund as the largest false advertising settlement on record.Claims close on December 21, but payments will wait until 2027The deadline to file is December 21, 2026. A federal district court in San Jose will hold the final approval hearing on February 24, 2027, and payments will only go out after that. Any appeal could delay them further.Anyone unsure about eligibility can call the settlement administrator on 1-888-988-8945. For those who bought an iPhone 16 waiting for the new Siri, the money will arrive even later than the feature did.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: How to find your lost Android phone using Google Find Hub
articles.summary: Lost your Android phone? Google's Find Hub is the first place to check, and you don't need a second Android device to use it.
articles.body: Lost your Android phone? Google's Find Hub is the first place to check, and you don't need a second Android device to use it. Any web browser, on a laptop or a friend's iPhone, can show you where your phone was last seen, make it ring, lock it, or wipe it clean.Find Hub is the new name for Google's Find My Device. It runs on an opt-in network of millions of Android devices that pick up Bluetooth signals from lost phones, earbuds and tracker tags, then quietly report their location back to the owner. That location data is end-to-end encrypted, so only you can see it. Google says it can't either.Set up Find Hub on your Android phone before you lose itFind Hub switches on automatically once you sign in with a Google account. But a few settings decide how useful it will be on the day your phone goes missing. Check these now:Location and Bluetooth are turned on"Allow device to be located" is enabled under the Find Hub settings (look under Security, or Google > All Services > Personal & Device Safety)Offline finding is set to "With network in busy places only" or "With network everywhere"A PIN, pattern or password is set, since offline finding won't work without oneYou're signed in to a Google account you can still accessNewer Pixel phones can even be located several hours after they've been switched off. Menu names vary a little by brand, but the options look similar on most Android phones.How to locate a lost Android phone on a mapOpen the Find Hub app on another Android phone or a Wear OS watch, or visit the Find Hub website on any browser. Sign in with the same Google account and pick your phone from the device list. The map shows its last known location, and you can get directions through Google Maps.If the phone is somewhere nearby, tap Play sound. It rings at full volume for five minutes, even on silent. Within 10 metres, the Find Nearby feature shows a shape that fills in as you get closer.Lock or erase your Android phone if it's stolenIf the phone is gone for good, act fast.Mark as lost: Locks the phone with your PIN and shows a message and contact number on the lock screen. On phones running Android 17 with fingerprint or Face Unlock, it adds two-step verification too. Keep the message short, as scammers can use those details to trick you into unlocking the phone for them.Remote Lock: No Google password handy? You can lock the screen using just your phone number.Factory reset: Your last resort. It permanently deletes everything and removes the phone from Find Hub, so you can't track it after that.Check those settings once, and the next time your phone goes missing, you'll know exactly where to look.You use AI every day. articles.title: Amid reports of Apple Pay launching in India next month, the iPhone-maker begins hiring for payments role
articles.summary: As Apple Pay launch in India nears, the company has a new job listing for a Business Development Manager - Wallet, Payments and Commerce.
articles.body: As Apple Pay launch in India nears, the company has a new job listing for a Business Development Manager - Wallet, Payments and Commerce. As per the job listing, the person hired for the role will “help grow and drive payment services as a part of Wallets, Payments & Commerce”. The iPhone-maker is expected to finally launch the Apple Pay in India next month, i.e October. A Reuters report previously stated that Apple may partner with Axis Bank as its first major banking partner in the country.What Apple Pay job listing in India saysAs per the listing, the individual will handle strategic commercial negotiations, partnerships, business development areas, as well as platform integration of Issuers, Acquirers and POS vendors for different Apple Pay product offerings onto the Apple Pay platform in India.“This is a role that works cross functionally with Technical Project Manager leads, Apple Pay Engineering, Operations, Privacy, Compliance, Legal and Product Marketing. Externally, it works with Banks, payment regulator, payment networks, acquirers, merchants, integrators, credential managers and software/hardware vendors to help define and deliver a wide variety of exiting Wallet solutions,” the listing says.The individual will manage all aspects of the partner relationship including; early engagement, account and project management, new product and feature introductions, commercial and contractual matters.“As a key member of the team, the incumbent will help sell a vision of the Wallet experience and consumer benefits to senior executives, successfully negotiate, close deals and lead the tactical execution to quickly grow our business in a sustainable way. He/she will work closely with our strategic partners to help develop best practice Wallet deployments and ensure that they are our primary development partners for new Wallet features. Internally, the individual will work with Apple product and engineering teams to influence product roadmap and provide feedback received from partners in the field”.Responsibilities will include:Establish, develop and grow strong business relationships with payment providers, banks, international and domestic payment networks etcClose commercial and contractual terms terms with partners in IndiaStay apprised of changing payments & regulatory landscape to make certain that the global strategy is aligned to meet local market needsMonitor performance of implemented solutions to establish outstanding service for customers and to find opportunities for partner improvementsDrive engagement of payment solutions ensuring all product and compliance requirements are metHelp drive substantive and measurable change in adoption rate, usage, penetration and scaleManage multiple parties and projects from initiation to completion while providing consistent updates and communication to business leadership.Apple Pay may launch in India next monthApple Pay could finally launch in India as early as October. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman stated in his Power On newsletter that Apple is preparing to launch Apple Pay in India “finally” next month. The service is expected to support card payments, while there are also reports that Apple could bring UPI support to the platform. The service was first launched in the US in 2014.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
